sources.note: Exact indexed id, imported name, approximate 1279 to 1492 interval and historical-basemaps provenance.

sources.title: Human History Map imported summaries
sources.note: Imported overview that correctly gestures toward historical Kediri but conflicts with the indexed interval and cannot repair the polygon.

sources.title: Human History Map 1200 borders
sources.note: Decoded preceding east-java feature, exact geometry comparison and point-owner tests during the actual Kediri period.

sources.title: Human History Map 1279 borders
sources.note: Decoded first exact kediri feature, topology, bounds, coordinate hash, islands and point tests.

sources.title: Human History Map 1300 borders
sources.note: Decoded second exact interval and verified geometry identity with the 1279 snapshot.

sources.title: Human History Map 1400 borders
sources.note: Decoded third exact interval, minute coordinate change, bounds, hash and repeated overextension.

sources.title: Human History Map 1492 borders
sources.note: Decoded target disappearance and historically impossible replacement of tested Java points by malaysian-islamic-states.

sources.title: P. E. de Josselin de Jong, The Character of the Hindu-Javanese State, Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis of Airlangga division, Kadiri dominance and Ken Angrok victory in 1222, used with its historiographic cautions.

sources.title: F. D. K. Bosch, The Old-Javanese Bathing Place Jalatunda, Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde
sources.note: Peer-reviewed chronology identifying Śrṅga or Kertajaya as the last Kadiri ruler and separating text traditions from securely dated inscriptions.

sources.title: Lydia Kieven, Following the Cap-Figure in Majapahit Temple Reliefs, Brill
sources.note: Scholarly political outline of Airlangga partition, Panjalu or Kediri, the 1222 transition to Singhasari and later Majapahit contexts.

sources.title: Arjunawiwāha: The Marriage of Arjuna of Mpu Kanwa, Brill introduction
sources.note: Scholarly introduction to Airlangga, the 1041 Pucangan inscription, 1042 retirement and division into Janggala and Panjalu.

sources.title: Mengenal Cerita Panji, Direktorat Warisan dan Diplomasi Budaya
sources.note: Official cultural-history discussion of Panjalu centered at Daha, Janggala and the later spread and many versions of Panji stories.

sources.title: Situs Besole: Sisa-sisa Kerajaan Kadiri, Berkala Arkeologi
sources.note: Official archaeological journal study of Kadiri inscriptions, ruler sequence, Daha and cautiously attributed brick remains at Besole.

sources.title: Gapura Plumbangan dan Sejarahnya, Balai Pelestarian Kebudayaan Wilayah XI
sources.note: Official heritage account of the 1120 Panumbangan inscription and Bameswara sima grant, while distinguishing the surviving gateway.

sources.title: Candi Panataran: Candi Kerajaan Masa Majapahit, official archaeology article
sources.note: Archaeological study separating the 1197 Śrṅga Palah inscription from the mostly later Majapahit sanctuary complex.

sources.title: The Figure of the Taṇḍa in Old Javanese Literary and Epigraphic Records, Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde
sources.note: Peer-reviewed comparison of elite warrior or guard titles in epigraphy and literature from Kediri through later periods.

sources.title: Titi Surti Nastiti, Perkembangan Aksara Kwadrat di Jawa Tengah, Jawa Timur, dan Bali, Kementerian Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan
sources.note: Official peer-reviewed epigraphic study of Hantang stone D 9, Jayabhaya, 1057 Śaka or 1135 CE and the quadrate phrase pañjalu jayati.

sources.title: Praśāsti, Direktorat Pelindungan Kebudayaan
sources.note: Official explanation of stone, copper and palm-leaf inscriptions as formal royal or high-official documents with sacred and legal force.

sources.title: Prasasti dan Citralekha, Balai Pelestarian Cagar Budaya Yogyakarta
sources.note: Official account of specialized inscription writers who mastered Old Javanese language, script, court formulae and bureaucracy.

sources.title: In Search of Lost Time: The Pāṇḍawa Story in the Javanese Cultural Tradition, Australian National University Open Research
sources.note: University research on Jayabhaya court literature, the Bhāratayuddha and creative Old Javanese adaptation rather than simple copying.

sources.title: Helen Creese, The Balinese Kakawin Tradition, Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde
sources.note: Peer-reviewed chronology of surviving East Javanese kakawin, patrons and poets, including Kediri works and later manuscript transmission.

sources.title: Traces of Śalyawadha in the Old Javanese Bhāratayuddha and Balinese Literature, Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of the 1157 Bhāratayuddha and later Balinese adaptations, used to keep composition distinct from surviving copies.

sources.title: Beberapa Prasasti yang Berisi tentang Irigasi Sawah, Direktorat Pelindungan Kebudayaan
sources.note: Official epigraphic survey of dams, dikes, reservoirs and channels, including Brantas flood control immediately before the Kediri partition.

sources.title: Berguru Pada Leluhur, Direktorat Warisan dan Diplomasi Budaya
sources.note: Official discussion of Airlangga 1037 Wringin Sapta dam, Brantas floods, boat traffic and water officials as close pre-Kediri infrastructure context.

sources.title: Tondowongso: Menyingkap Peradaban Kediri, Kementerian Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan repository
sources.note: Official archaeological monograph on the Tondowongso brick sanctuary, its eleventh to thirteenth-century horizon, layout, sculpture and research limits.

sources.title: Arca-arca dari Situs Tondowongso dan Gurah, Berkala Arkeologi
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeological study of Brahma, Candra, Surya, Nandi and yoni finds and the limits of unfinished site research.

sources.title: Lesley Pullen, Kediri and Singhasāri: Stone Sculpture from the Eleventh to the Fourteenth Century, Cambridge University Press
sources.note: Scholarly art-history chapter stressing how little securely attributable Kediri sculpture survives and discussing the debated Boro Gaṇeśa.

sources.title: Zhao Rugua, Zhufan zhi, translated by Hirth and Rockhill as Chau Ju-Kua, Cornell University Library scan
sources.note: Primary thirteenth-century Chinese compilation on Java trade, farming, clothing, entertainment, government and healing, read with geographic and reporting cautions.

sources.title: The Lingwai Daida of Zhou Qufei: A Translation and Critical Edition, University of Tuscia repository
sources.note: University-hosted annotated translation of a 1178 geographic work explaining that information often came through traders, sailors and earlier texts.

sources.title: Judith H. Maxwell, Texts and Textiles in Medieval Java, Bulletin de l’École française d’Extrême-Orient
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis of textiles as valued goods, literary images and sima-charter evidence, with explicit source-survival cautions.

sources.title: Helen Creese, Subhadrāwiwāha: an Old Javanese kakawin, Australian National University Open Research
sources.note: University thesis on marriage forms and ceremonies in Old Javanese kakawin, while dating this particular poem much later than Kediri.

sources.title: Muhamad Alnoza and Dian Sulistyowati, Konstruksi Masyarakat Jawa Kuno terhadap Transgender Perempuan, AMERTA
sources.note: Peer-reviewed epigraphic table including Kediri-period Padlĕgan I and Kĕmulan occupational terms, walyan healers and sima administrative structure.

proposedOverrides.summary: Historical Kediri or Panjalu, circa 1042 to 1222; the indexed 1279 to 1492 display interval is erroneous.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact imported id kediri is preserved, while public copy identifies the historical Kediri or Panjalu kingdom and dates it circa 1042 to 1222.
The indexed 1279 to 1492 interval is impossible for historical Kediri and overlaps the Singhasari aftermath and Majapahit era.
The preceding east-java record is a generic regional bucket and is not aliased to Kediri, Janggala or Singhasari.
Majapahit remains a separately carded coverage record. Later Daha or Kediri identities are not merged into Panjalu without evidence.
The imported geometry includes southern Borneo and eastern Sumbawa, omits the Brantas delta and key north-coast ports, and cannot be treated as sovereignty.
The 1492 malaysian-islamic-states replacement is an impossible atlas seam. The override keeps fell null and provides no inferred successor.
Historical periods cover 1042 to 1222 rather than allowing the atlas error to overwrite the kingdom chronology.
The authentic written sample is the 1135 Hantang phrase pañjalu jayati, shown in scholarly transliteration with original-glyph facsimile limits.
